entries.unverified: attempted on Claude Code 2.1.266 through the hardened record.sh (nocx-nru89.8): (1) the new claude-2.1.266-turn capture's real generation never stalled, so the chrome did not occur naturally within it (unlike the nocx-nru89.7 recording, where it appeared incidentally at 72000ms during a real slow LM Studio response); (2) recorded against the SKILL.md never-answering listener (127.0.0.1:18999, accept-and-never-respond) with the lmstudio-api.script procedure, first with its documented 40s final wait (claude-2.1.266-api-waiting.jsonl, 291 chunks) and again with the wait extended to 190s (same file, 1251 chunks, ~228s of real elapsed time total, just under record.sh's 240s hard capture ceiling): in both runs the screen never advances past a plain, ever-growing spinner ('· Manifesting… (3m 10s)', cycling through Claude's usual spinner glyphs, by the end of the second run) -- the TUI is still treating the request as in flight and never draws 'Waiting for API response · will retry in' or any 'check your network' text. The old claude-lmstudio-turn@72000 entry (kept above) is the only evidence this corpus has of the owner's api-waiting chrome; awaiting owner decision on whether a longer wait (beyond what one record.sh invocation's 240s ceiling allows) reproduces it, or whether the chrome needs an actual mid-request network failure rather than a connection that is accepted and then never answered.
